name: Adams County
tax_rate: 2% special hotel-motel tax in unincorporated Adams County (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer); Adams County Code 3.14, Ord. O-3-98, effective July 1, 1998
notes: Adams County Code chapter 3.14 puts the 2% lodging tax into a 'tourism enhancement fund' for advertising and visitor promotion but creates no advisory committee and no application process. DOR Table L1 shows the county received only $815 in 2024 because nearly all lodging in the county is inside Othello and Ritzville, which levy their own taxes. There is no county grant program; events in the county should look to the City of Othello LTAC or Ritzville.
pool_note: 2024 county lodging tax receipts were $815 per DOR Table L1; nothing is awarded to outside applicants.

funding_docs.title: Adams County Code Chapter 3.14 Special Excise Tax on Lodging
funding_docs.summary: Levies a 2% lodging tax and directs proceeds to a non-lapsing tourism enhancement fund for advertising and promotion under RCW 67.28; no advisory committee or application process.

alternatives.funds: Not researched for this record; Othello is the largest lodging market in Adams County
alternatives.notes: Othello's LTAC is the only active lodging tax program in Adams County found online.

name: Asotin
tax_rate: 2% special hotel-motel tax, location code 0201 (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer)
notes: The City of Asotin (pop. about 1,200) levies the 2% lodging tax but its 2024 receipts are suppressed as confidential in DOR Table L1, meaning fewer than three lodging taxpayers; the city reported no lodging tax spending to JLARC for 2022-2024. No LTAC, application or grant program appears on the city website or in search results. Use the Asotin County Lodging Tax Grant for an event in or near Asotin.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Table L1, 2024 local lodging tax distributions

alternatives.administrator: Asotin County Board of Commissioners / Lodging Tax Advisory Committee
alternatives.funds: County received $189,088 in 2024 lodging tax distributions (DOR Table L1); grant pool not published
alternatives.eligibility: Tourism promotion projects in Asotin County; online application form on the county website
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Application window September 1 to September 30 for the following year (2024 cycle posted); 2026 window not confirmed online
alternatives.notes: The City of Clarkston also runs its own lodging tax distribution (2025: Visit Lewis-Clark Valley $145,000, Valley Vision $10,000, Asotin County Family Aquatic Center $25,000 per Lewiston Tribune, Dec. 2024), but that is for Clarkston projects. Visit Lewis-Clark Valley is the regional DMO.
alternatives.contact: Asotin County Commissioners' office via asotincountywa.gov (no named grant contact posted)

name: La Center
tax_rate: 2% special hotel-motel tax, location code 0603 (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer)
notes: La Center levies the 2% lodging tax but its 2024 receipts are confidential in DOR Table L1 (fewer than three taxpayers; the ilani casino hotel sits on Cowlitz tribal trust land outside the city tax base) and it reported no lodging tax spending to JLARC for 2022-2024. No LTAC page, application or award history was found on ci.lacenter.wa.us or in council records. Treat as no program; Clark County itself also has no open grant process, so Visit Vancouver WA marketing support is the practical route.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Table L1, 2024 local lodging tax distributions

alternatives.administrator: Clark County Council / County Manager's Office
alternatives.funds: County received $2,028,908 in 2024 lodging tax distributions (DOR Table L1); no published competitive grant pool found
alternatives.eligibility: No open application process found online; county lodging tax has historically supported the county tourism contract (Visit Vancouver WA) and county facilities rather than outside grants
alternatives.notes: Clark County does not post an LTAC grant application page; events in north Clark County typically seek sponsorship through Visit Vancouver WA or the City of Vancouver LTAC program (city limits only). Confirm with the County Manager's Office.

alternatives.eligibility: Tourism events and attractions in Clark County
alternatives.notes: Best first call for marketing help for a north Clark County event.

name: McCleary
tax_rate: 3% special hotel-motel tax, location code 1405 (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer); city budget books it as 'Hotel/Motel Stadium Tax' in the Current Expense fund
notes: McCleary's lodging tax is effectively nil: the 2020 city budget (council packet Nov. 13, 2019) shows $0 collected 2016-2018, $32.34 in 2019 and $30 budgeted for 2020, booked straight into the Current Expense fund with no tourism fund or committee. 2024 DOR distributions are confidential. Because McCleary levies a 3% tax of its own, note that Grays Harbor County's tourism grant excludes projects located in cities that manage their own 3% lodging tax, so a McCleary-sited event should confirm eligibility with the county tourism office before applying.
pool_note: City budget shows roughly $30 a year in lodging tax; nothing is available to applicants.

funding_docs.title: McCleary City Council packet, November 13, 2019 (2020 preliminary budget)
funding_docs.summary: Shows Hotel/Motel Stadium Tax revenue of $0 for 2016-2018, $32.34 in 2019 and $30 proposed for 2020 in the Current Expense fund; no lodging tax fund, committee or grants.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Table L1, 2024 local lodging tax distributions

alternatives.program: Grays Harbor County Tourism Hospitality Services and Special Projects Grant (lodging tax funded)
alternatives.administrator: Grays Harbor County Department of Tourism (Grays Harbor Tourism), 32 Elma-McCleary Road, Elma
alternatives.funds: Up to $100,000 available in the category for 2027, maximum $20,000 per application; a separate Major Tourism Project Grant exists for larger capital/attraction projects
alternatives.eligibility: Tax-exempt nonprofits (501(c)(3), 501(c)(6)) and government agencies that do not collect their own 3% lodging tax; projects in cities that manage their own lodging tax (which includes McCleary at 3%) are excluded, so a McCleary-located event may be ineligible; confirm with the tourism office
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications accepted August 15 to September 15 each year for the following year; mailed or hand-delivered only
alternatives.notes: County collected $2,986,793 in 2024 lodging tax (DOR Table L1). Grant workshop held in August.
alternatives.contact: Grays Harbor Tourism, PO Box 1229, Elma, WA 98541, (800) 621-9625

name: Milton
tax_rate: 2% lodging excise tax (Pierce County portion, RCW 67.28.180) and 2% special excise tax on lodging with 59 or fewer units in the King County portion (Milton Municipal Code 3.17); DOR location code 2709
notes: Milton Municipal Code chapter 3.17 levies the tax, creates a lodging tax fund and provides for a five-member LTAC (council chair, two lodging collectors, two recipients), but the city has almost no lodging: DOR Table L1 shows $2,033 distributed in 2024 and the city reported no spending to JLARC for 2022-2024. No LTAC roster, application or awards appear on cityofmilton.net. Milton is expressly within the Pierce County Lodging Tax Grant Program's eligible area, which is the real funding route.
pool_note: 2024 receipts of $2,033 per DOR Table L1; no grant pool.

funding_docs.title: Milton Municipal Code Chapter 3.17 Lodging Tax
funding_docs.summary: Levies 2% lodging taxes in the Pierce and King County portions of the city, establishes a lodging tax fund for tourism promotion under RCW 67.28, and provides for a five-member lodging tax advisory committee; no application process described.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Table L1, 2024 local lodging tax distributions

alternatives.program: Pierce County Lodging Tax Grant Program
alternatives.funds: 2027 cycle pool $5,308,730 across six categories (Event Marketing and Operations $540,000; Event Development $118,730; Sports Event Development $60,000; Individual Leisure Marketing $1,500,000; Asset/Product Development $2,290,000; Personnel and Administration $800,000)
alternatives.eligibility: Municipalities and 501(c)(3)/501(c)(6) organizations at least one year old; projects must benefit lodging in areas paying into the county lodging tax, which expressly includes Milton and Orting (only Fife, Gig Harbor, Lakewood, Puyallup and Tacoma are excluded); a one-on-one meeting with staff is required before submitting
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications for the following year open in early June and close in early July (June 4 to July 3, 2026 for 2027 funds); LTAC meets about four times a year
alternatives.notes: County LTAC has 12 members chaired by a County Council member. 2024 county lodging tax distributions were $5.44 million (DOR Table L1).
alternatives.contact: Mike Gommi, Pierce County Economic Development, mike.gommi@piercecountywa.gov; department line (253) 798-6150

pool_note: 2024 receipts of $393 per DOR Table L1; no grant pool.

name: Pomeroy
tax_rate: 2% special excise tax on lodging (Pomeroy Municipal Code 3.10, Ord. 834, 2007); DOR rate flyer lists no special hotel-motel code for Pomeroy
notes: Pomeroy Municipal Code chapter 3.10 levies a 2% lodging tax into a general fund sub-account for advertising and tourism under RCW 67.28 but creates no advisory committee or application process. DOR Table L1 shows $864 distributed in 2024 and the city reported no spending to JLARC for 2022-2024. Garfield County received $0, so there is no county program either; the Pomeroy Chamber of Commerce and Garfield County Fair are the local event partners.

name: Ridgefield
tax_rate: 2% special hotel-motel tax, location code 0604 (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer)

name: South Cle Elum
tax_rate: 2% special hotel-motel tax, location code 1905 (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer)
notes: South Cle Elum levies the 2% lodging tax; DOR Table L1 shows $0 for 2024 with components suppressed as confidential (the Iron Horse Inn B&B is the main lodging), and the town reported no spending to JLARC for 2022-2024. No LTAC, application or awards were found. Kittitas County's CLTAC program is a joint fund of the county and the cities of Cle Elum, Ellensburg and Roslyn; South Cle Elum is not a listed participant, so confirm with the County Auditor whether a South Cle Elum event (which draws county-wide overnight stays) can apply.
pool_note: 2024 receipts suppressed as confidential in DOR Table L1; no grant pool.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Table L1, 2024 local lodging tax distributions
funding_docs.summary: South Cle Elum 2024 total distribution $0 (two components confidential).

alternatives.program: Kittitas County Lodging Tax Fund (CLTAC) grants
alternatives.administrator: Kittitas County Auditor's Office (joint program of Kittitas County and the cities of Cle Elum, Ellensburg and Roslyn)
alternatives.funds: Pool not stated on the guide page; county distributions were $2,623,195 in 2024 (DOR Table L1); ongoing events capped at 10% of expense budget
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofits (501(c)(3), 501(c)(6)) and public entities for tourism marketing, events and festivals, and tourism facilities; South Cle Elum is not listed as a participating city, so confirm with the Auditor whether a South Cle Elum event qualifies (events are scored on county-wide tourism impact)
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications due mid-September (September 18, 2026, 4 pm) for the following year; workshops in mid-August; oral presentations to CLTAC in late November (November 20, 2026)
alternatives.notes: Minimum average score of 50 points; preference for projects that increase overnight stays and show a path to self-sustainability.
